headline: Quantitative metrics for protein structure, binding sites, and low-complexity regions
label: Biomolecular Structure Analysis Methods
summary: Explicit, parameterized metrics now replace single-scale descriptions across disordered proteins, binding sites, fungal allergens, and sequence repeats.
synthesis: The common thread is a move toward explicit, parameterized metrics for describing protein structure and sequence features. A data-driven stickiness scale for the 20 amino acids was derived from biophysical data on 115 disordered proteins and compared against 70 hydropathy scales. Binding site vectors integrate shape and electrostatics to compare protein binding sites across over 600 CYP entries. A structure-based manifold framework embeds 150 fungal allergens using AlphaFold TM-score distances, with epitope-level analysis. A benchmark of eight low-complexity region detection methods across the human proteome compares length, coverage, entropy, and consensus patterns. These items are methodologically heterogeneous, so the shared element is the emphasis on explicit metrics rather than a single unified finding.
